title: Farm Real Estate Loans — Reversal of Returned Payments and the Returned Payment Fee
content:
A returned payment on a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage is reversed row by row: each return entry carries the original entry's amount and effective date and points to the original entry, so the installment it paid is reopened.

## Rules

- **Reversed once.** A payment may be reversed only once; whether it has already been reversed is read from the loan's transaction record — a return entry already pointing to the same payment.
- **Returned payment fee.** One returned payment fee, at the product's returned payment fee, is assessed per returned remittance, booked from the principal return entry.
- **Unauthorized returns.** No returned payment fee is assessed when the bank's return reason is unauthorized.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A remittance of USD 6000.00 was applied as USD 2500.00 to an installment's billed interest and USD 3500.00 to its principal share. The bank returns it for insufficient funds.

| Original entry | Return entry | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| interest payment USD 2500.00 | interest return USD 2500.00, same effective date, pointing to it | billed interest owed rises by 2500.00 |
| principal payment USD 3500.00 | principal return USD 3500.00, same effective date, pointing to it | principal rises by 3500.00 |

The installment is reopened. One returned payment fee is assessed for the remittance, booked from the principal return entry. Had the return reason been unauthorized, the two return entries would stand and no fee would be assessed. A second return of the same payments is not made.
